title: How a Keyboard Works in 60 Seconds ⌨️⚡ #shorts
description:
Your keyboard doesn't give every key its own wire. The keys sit on a grid of rows and columns, and pressing one squashes a rubber dome that pushes two membrane layers together, connecting one row to one column. A tiny controller scans the grid row by row many times a second, finds the crossing, and sends that key's code to your computer. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#keyboard #computer #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Your keyboard doesn't give every key its own wire. It uses a *grid*.

steps.label: Matrix
steps.text: Under the keys, traces run in *rows* and *columns*, and every key sits where two of them cross.

steps.label: Press
steps.text: Press a key, and a *rubber dome* squashes, pushing two thin *membrane* layers together.

steps.label: Contact
steps.text: Their printed pads touch, *connecting* that row to that column.

steps.label: Scan
steps.text: A tiny *controller* powers one row at a time, many times a second, and checks which *column* lights up.

steps.label: Send
steps.text: It turns that crossing into a *key code* and sends it to your *computer*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Press, connect, *scan*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
